reasons: The cited Section 19 text supports the compliant classification: 19.1 gives a professional/workmanlike and material-conformance warranty, 19.2 provides ninety days from delivery or acceptance for Deliverables and conformance throughout the subscription term for Hosted Services (meeting/exceeding the preferred 90-day services and 12-month software benchmarks), 19.3 adds malicious-code and Applicable Law warranties, and 19.4 supplies the preferred re-perform/repair/replace/refund remedy.

The disclaimer in 19.5 is mutual, limited to implied warranties, and expressly does not limit any express warranty or stated remedy, so there is no risk of the disclaimer swallowing the express warranty and no 'AS IS' walk-away exposure.

The failed deterministic period check is correctly diagnosed as a false negative — the period is spelled in words ('ninety days') rather than digits — so it does not undercut the compliance conclusion.

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline was proposed and no counterparty comment was added; the redline text is identical to the original paragraphs. The narrower 'intentionally introduced by Vendor' malicious-code scope is properly noted as a minor sub-element in the rationale rather than flagged as a deviation.
